subject: Incident: Hosted API generation stall — customer summary and immediate mitigations
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@novacredit.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Incident: Hosted API generation stall — customer summary and immediate mitigations

Hi Alex,

I wanted to reach out directly with a concise summary of the incident we observed this morning affecting NovaCredit traffic and what we have done to reduce impact. We've also published the incident on our status page (link below) and will follow with a technical postmortem once the timeline and root cause analysis are complete.

What happened (brief)
- Between ~08:42 and ~09:08 PST we observed an elevated rate of generation stalls and long-tail p99/p999 latency for hosted text-generation requests routed to model redwood-rlm-large. The symptom was requests that either returned partial content or experienced extended inference retries leading to increased client timeouts for a subset of request patterns.

Immediate mitigations applied
- Activated routing fallback to redwood-rlm-medium for NovaCredit traffic at 08:50 PST (reduced p99 by ~60% for affected requests).
- Applied a short burst limit on concurrent generation sessions to reduce retry amplification.
- Temporarily disabled aggressive prefetch on warm pools for the affected capacity group to reduce KV contention.
- Rolled a targeted config patch (kernel selection parameter) through the control plane at 09:00 PST; this reduced residual error rates.

Impact to you
- Affected traffic window: ~08:42 - 09:08 PST.
- Approximately 0.4% of NovaCredit production requests received partial responses or exceeded your client timeout thresholds during the peak.
- We do not believe any user data was exposed or altered.

Attachments and links
- Attached: incident_timeline_20261113.pdf (quick chronology) and sample_requests_20261113.ndjson (anonymized request traces).
- Status page: https://status.redwood.inference/incidents/2026-11-13-gen-stall-7h3k
- Internal logs/export: https://drive.redwood.com/novacredit/incident-logs-20261113 (read-only link)

Next steps
- We're continuing analysis on root cause (likely kernel selection + rare KV eviction race under a specific sequence-length/profile).
- I'll schedule a short technical call with your engineering team for 1600 PST today if that works — we can walk the timeline, logs, and planned remediation (configuration + longer-term runtime change).
- Postmortem and proposed mitigations (including rollback and routing policy changes) by EOD Monday, 2026-11-16.

If you want immediate help or would like us to pause routing to the large variant for a longer period, let me know and we can do that. Apologies for the disruption — we know availability and correctness are critical for NovaCredit.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Incident: Hosted API generation stall — customer summary and immediate mitigations

Thanks Ben — appreciate the fast summary and the status page link. A couple quick questions: 

1) Do you plan to issue SLA credits for the impacted window? Our billing/contact point is watching the request-counts and will want an estimate.
2) Can you confirm whether any of the requests that returned partial responses included streaming tokens that were later resumed (we saw a couple of client-side retries leading to duplicated events)?
3) The proposed 1600 PST call is OK for our on-call engineer; can you send a calendar invite?

- Marissa: please pull an estimate of impacted request counts and the billing impact window (08:42–09:08 PST) and propose an SLA credit calculation by 12:30 PST. Attach straightforward numbers we can share with Alex.
- Laura: can you confirm whether our logs show resumed streaming tokens leading to duplicate downstream events for NovaCredit? If yes, capture an example pair and one-line explanation of the mechanism.
- Engineering notes: Marissa and I already included a short anonymized trace (sample_requests_20261113.ndjson) in the public read-only folder; we may need deeper traces from prod-infer-2 (request ids: included in the file).

I'll create the 16:00 PST invite and include Service Reliability and Product; please ping me on Slack if you hit blockers.

Ben
